intro: To create a bulleted list in Pages on Mac, type a dash and a space, type your first item, and press Return. To turn text you have already typed into bullets, select it, click Style in the Format sidebar, and choose a style from the Bullets & Lists menu.
tldr: Type a dash and a space, then your first item, and press Return. Pages starts the next line with a bullet.
For text you already wrote, select it, then click Style in the Format sidebar and pick from Bullets & Lists.
Press Tab to indent and Shift-Tab to move back out. Press Return twice or Delete to end the list.
If dashes do not become bullets, check Pages > Settings > Auto-Correction for Automatically detect lists.

blocks.text: Bullets in Pages look simple until the dash does nothing. Apple's Pages guide for Mac gives two routes. The first is automatic. You type a dash, Pages recognizes the pattern, and each new line gets the same marker. The second is manual. You select text you already wrote and apply a bullet style from the Format sidebar. Learn the automatic route first, then use the manual one for anything already on the page. One setting controls the automatic route, and you will find it later in this guide.
Create a bulleted list automatically in Pages on Mac

Start on the line where the list should begin. Type a dash, then a space, then your first item. Press Return. Pages starts the next line with a bullet, so you keep typing. When the list is finished, press Return twice, or press Delete, to leave it. Apple's guide says a number or a letter followed by a period and a space works the same way. Pages then continues the pattern on each new line. Check the first two items on screen before you type the rest, since a wrong start is easier to fix early.

items: Type a dash, then a space, to start a bulleted list.
Type each item and press Return to add the next bullet.
Press Tab to indent an item into a sub-bullet.
Press Shift-Tab to move an item back out.
Press Return twice, or press Delete, to end the list.

blocks.text: Apple's guide also lists Option-8 as a way to insert a bullet. Press ⌥8 where you want the marker, then type your item. Use it when the dash does not do what you expect. If the list still does not continue on the next line, check the Auto-Correction setting before you try again. Both routes end the same way, with Return twice or Delete. Option-8 is the only shortcut Apple lists for a bullet character in Pages on Mac.

The same automatic method makes a numbered list. Type a number or a letter, then a period and a space, and then your first item. Pages continues the sequence on each new line. Use numbers when order matters, such as steps in a process. Use bullets when order does not matter, such as a list of features to check. You can switch between the two later, so the choice does not lock you in.
Turn existing text into bullets with the Format sidebar

Use this method when the words are already on the page. Select the paragraphs you want as bullets. Open the Format sidebar, click Style, and find the Bullets & Lists pop-up menu. Choose a list style from the menu. Each selected paragraph becomes a bullet. If the result is wrong, press ⌘Z to undo, then select the text again and try a different style.

blocks.text: Text inside a text box, a table, or a shape follows the same steps with one change. Select the text, click the Text tab in the Format sidebar, and then click Style. Skip the Text tab and the Bullets & Lists control may not appear where you expect it. In a table, select the words in the cell rather than the whole cell, so the style applies only to the text you meant to change.
Indent, change the bullet style, and end a list

Indentation sets the structure of the list. Put the cursor at the start of an item and press Tab to move it one level in. Press Shift-Tab to move it back out. Apple's guide describes these keys for lists on Mac, and they work the same way for numbered items. Plan the levels before you type, because fixing each line one at a time is slow. Keep sub-bullets short and specific so the parent item stays easy to scan.

To change the bullet itself, select the list items, open Style, and click the disclosure arrow next to Bullets & Lists. The pop-up below it offers Text Bullets, Image Bullets, and Numbers. Text Bullets uses a character. Image Bullets uses a picture. Numbers turns the list into a numbered one. Pick a single style for the whole list so the page stays consistent from top to bottom.
Fix lists that do not start automatically in Pages

Start with the setting. Choose Pages > Settings, click Auto-Correction, and make sure Automatically detect lists is selected. Deselect it if you want Pages to stop turning typed dashes and numbers into lists. An Apple Community user on macOS 13.6 said the setting was already on and automatic lists still did not form. That thread closed without a confirmed fix. Use the Format sidebar method as your backup.
Which Pages version you are running on your Mac

Apple's Mac list guide does not name a Pages or macOS version. Apple's Pages support page does not list a current version number either. MacRumors reported on January 28, 2026 that the older Pages app on Mac was updated to 14.5 only to say it no longer receives new features. The separate Apple Creator Studio edition is version 15.1. Open Pages from your Applications folder and check which app you are running before you follow any tutorial, this one included.

Creator Studio is a paid subscription. MacRumors reports $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S. Check Apple's own pricing before you subscribe, because prices can change after that report. The stats below come from that same report.
Bullets in Pages for iCloud

Pages for iCloud runs in a browser at icloud.com/pages, and its list steps are close to the Mac steps. Select the text, click Style in the Format sidebar, and open the Bullets & Lists pop-up. Choose None from that menu to end a list. Apple's iCloud guide does not list a keyboard shortcut for creating lists beyond pressing Return or Enter twice. Test ⌥8 in your browser before you depend on it, because browsers can handle keys differently.
A worked example: meeting notes with two levels

Say you are writing notes from a planning meeting. Type a dash, a space, and Decisions, then press Return. Press Tab and type the first decision, then press Return. Press Shift-Tab to return to the top level and type the next topic. Tab sets the level, so the lines line up without any extra spaces. Paste the notes into an email only after you check the layout, because pasted formatting does not always carry over cleanly.
Mistakes that waste time

A few habits cause most of the trouble in practice. The first is pressing Return once at the end of a list and then wondering why another bullet appears. Press Return twice, or press Delete, instead. The second is pasting text from a web page and expecting the list style to come along. Select the pasted lines and apply the style again. The third is looking for Bullets & Lists in a text box without clicking the Text tab first.
What to do next

Open a document with real content and try the automatic method first. Then select a paragraph you already wrote and apply a style from the sidebar. Once both feel routine, move on to the next formatting job. The guide on [how to add page numbers in Pages on Mac](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-pages) covers a common task after lists. The page on [how to create a table of contents in Pages on Mac](/how-to/create-a-table-of-contents-in-pages) helps when your bullets sit inside a long report.

If you send the file to someone else, check the list on their computer. A different app or version can show spacing and markers a little differently. If the layout must stay fixed, export a copy as a PDF and send that instead of the editable file.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for bullets in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's guide lists ⌥8 (Option-8) for inserting a bullet character. It does not list a shortcut for list styles, though it says one can be assigned, without explaining how.

faq.question: How do I make a numbered list instead of a bulleted one?
faq.answer: Type a number or a letter, then a period and a space, and then your first item. Pages continues the sequence on each new line. Apple's guide covers this in the same section as bullets.

faq.question: How do I turn off automatic lists in Pages?
faq.answer: Choose Pages > Settings, click Auto-Correction, and deselect Automatically detect lists. After that, Pages stops creating lists from typed dashes and numbers.

faq.question: Why does the Bullets & Lists menu do nothing on my text?
faq.answer: Check that you selected the text, not just placed the cursor. In a text box, table, or shape, click the Text tab in the Format sidebar first, then click Style.

faq.question: How do I end a bulleted list in Pages?
faq.answer: Press Return twice, or press Delete. In Pages for iCloud, choose None from the Bullets & Lists menu instead.

faq.question: Do these steps work in Pages for iCloud?
faq.answer: Mostly. The web version also uses Style and the Bullets & Lists pop-up in the Format sidebar. Apple's iCloud guide lists no extra shortcut beyond pressing Return or Enter twice.

task: Create a bulleted list in Pages on Mac
appliesTo: Pages on Mac, following the steps in Apple's Format lists guide
requirements: A document open with some text on the page
Access to Pages > Settings if automatic lists do not form

steps.name: Place the cursor where the list starts
steps.text: Click on the blank line where you want the list. If the line already has text, press Return first so the list starts on its own line.
steps.tip: You can build a list inside a text box too, but click inside the box first.

steps.name: Type a dash and a space
steps.text: Type a dash, then press the Space bar. Pages reads that pattern as the start of a bulleted list and adds a bullet at the cursor.
steps.tip: A number or a letter, a period, and a space starts a numbered list the same way.

steps.name: Type your first item and press Return
steps.text: Type the first item, then press Return. Pages starts the next line with a bullet. Keep typing and pressing Return for each item.

steps.name: Indent items to make sub-bullets
steps.text: Press Tab at the start of an item to move it one level in. Press Shift-Tab to move it back out. Use these keys instead of spaces so the levels stay consistent.

steps.name: End the list
steps.text: Press Return twice to leave the list and return to normal text. You can also press Delete to remove the empty bullet and stop the list.
steps.tip: If a bullet appears where you did not want one, press Delete once and check the cursor position.

steps.name: Select text you already wrote
steps.text: Drag across the paragraphs you want as bullets. You can also click in the first paragraph and Shift-click the last one. Every selected paragraph gets the bullet style.

steps.name: Open Style in the Format sidebar
steps.text: Open the Format sidebar, then click Style. For text in a text box, table, or shape, click the Text tab first, then click Style.
steps.tip: If the sidebar is hidden, click Format in the toolbar to show it.

steps.name: Pick a style from Bullets & Lists
steps.text: Click the Bullets & Lists pop-up menu and choose a list style. Later, click the disclosure arrow next to Bullets & Lists to switch between Text Bullets, Image Bullets, and Numbers.
steps.tip: Choose one style for the whole list so the page looks consistent.

shortcuts.action: Move a list item back out

troubleshooting.problem: Dash does not turn into a bullet
troubleshooting.fix: Check Pages > Settings > Auto-Correction and confirm Automatically detect lists is selected. Retype the dash and a space, or use ⌥8. If it still fails, apply the list style from the Format sidebar instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Bullets & Lists is missing from the sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Select the text first. If the text is in a text box, table, or shape, click the Text tab before you open Style. If the sidebar is hidden, click Format in the toolbar.
Press Return twice on the empty bullet, or press Delete. Apple's guide describes both ways to end a list.

troubleshooting.problem: Pasted text does not look like a list
troubleshooting.fix: Select the pasted lines and choose a style from the Bullets & Lists pop-up in the Style section. Pasted text can carry formatting from the source page.

troubleshooting.problem: The bullet style you want is not in the menu
troubleshooting.fix: Your Pages version may differ from the one Apple's guide describes. Check which app you are running, then look at Text Bullets, Image Bullets, and Numbers under the disclosure arrow.
